skipped: 4 test files, +727 lines (gesture_test.go +213, report_test.go +210, payload_test.go +188, session_test.go +116), used as evidence not walked; keys.go, 157 lines, HID usage constants + ASCII lookup table; report.go, 111 lines, byte layouts pinned by 4 tests in report_test.go; payload.go:5-40, 36 lines, HID report descriptor blob

stops.title: Why a HID package reaches for a video stream

claims.text: a report is fire-and-forget: SendReport returns once xpc Send has encoded and written the message, nothing reads a reply, so nil means written not acted on
claims.evidence: traced SendReport -> conn.Send -> EncodeMessage at ios/xpc/xpc.go:53-68

claims.text: nothing in UniversalConnection gates touch on a media stream; the gate lives entirely in Session
claims.evidence: hid.go has no stream reference; ios/hid is the only importer of ios/display

claims.text: the file states two different minimum iOS versions, 27+ in the package doc and 17+ on NewUniversal, and I did not establish which is right
claims.evidence: hid.go:2 vs hid.go:34, and session.go:88

claims.text: SurfaceKeyboardDefault is a value this package invents while 257 and 1281 are enumerated by the device
claims.evidence: comment at hid.go:25-27; never observed against a device in this session

stops.title: Session: what it owns and the two things it remembers

claims.text: streamLost is the only field written without the mutex, because the drain goroutine writes it while a gesture holds the lock
claims.evidence: atomic.Bool at session.go:74, written at session.go:407 from the goroutine

claims.text: a closed session fails every entry point instead of dereferencing released connections
claims.evidence: TestClosedSessionRejectsEverything

claims.text: Close on a session that never opened anything is safe and idempotent
claims.evidence: TestCloseOnUnopenedSessionIsSafe

claims.text: the hidConn and streamStopper interfaces exist so gestures can be exercised without a device
claims.evidence: fakeHID and stubStream in gesture_test.go implement exactly these two

stops.title: ensureStream: three orderings inside one negotiation

claims.text: the drain goroutine starts before StartVideoStream, so packets arriving the instant the device answers are already being read
claims.evidence: goroutine at session.go:402 precedes the call at session.go:416

claims.text: streamAnswer is stored before the error is checked, so a failed negotiation that still brought a stream up can be stopped later
claims.evidence: session.go:422 assigns before the err check at session.go:423

claims.text: a userspace tunnel is refused and leaves no stream state behind
claims.evidence: TestUserspaceTunnelIsRejectedForStreams

claims.text: 300ms is long enough for the surfaces to re-match after the stream starts
claims.evidence: nothing reports that state; the delay was never measured in this session

claims.text: re-negotiation churn wedges dtuhidd, which is why the settle sleep is not tied to ctx
claims.evidence: never reproduced on purpose; recovery is believed to be a device reboot

stops.title: teardownStream: the ordering that deadlocks if reversed

claims.text: the receiver socket is closed before the wait on drainDone; reversed, teardown blocks forever on a goroutine parked in a UDP read
claims.evidence: session.go:452-461; Receiver.Drain loops on a blocking ReadFromUDP at ios/display/receiver.go:77-89

claims.text: Drain returns nil on net.ErrClosed, so a normal teardown logs nothing
claims.evidence: ios/display/receiver.go:81-83 maps net.ErrClosed to nil

claims.text: stopStream is skipped entirely when the answer carries no ClientSessionID
claims.evidence: uuid.Nil guard at session.go:441

claims.text: the retry over a fresh connection is required because a timed-out negotiation has already closed its own connection
claims.evidence: reasoning from the comment at session.go:467-469; not run against a device in this session

stops.title: stroke: where the release lands when a sample fails

claims.text: a stroke releases where the contact actually is, not at the last requested point
claims.evidence: TestStrokeReleasesWhereTheContactActuallyIs

claims.text: Drag sends one sample more than its steps, the touch-down UIKit hit-tests plus one per step
claims.evidence: TestDragSendsOneSampleMoreThanItsSteps

claims.text: duration is spread evenly across the path rather than applied per sample
claims.evidence: TestStrokeSpreadsItsDurationAcrossThePath

claims.text: the release is a deferred send whose error is logged, not returned, so a gesture can return nil having failed to lift the contact
claims.evidence: session.go:174-182 logs via golog.Warn and returns nothing

stops.title: The contact ledger: which gestures Close can clean up after

claims.text: TouchUp with nothing down sends nothing and does not error
claims.evidence: TestTouchUpWithNothingDownSendsNothing and TestTouchUpWithoutDownIsNoop

claims.text: Close lifts a contact left down by an interrupted input stream before tearing anything down
claims.evidence: TestCloseLiftsAContactLeftDown

claims.text: only TouchDown and TouchMove record s.contactDown; Tap, Drag and Stroke track their contact in a local, so a Tap whose release fails leaves the device touched with nothing recording it
claims.evidence: sendContact at session.go:305 is the only writer; Tap at session.go:109-122 sets nothing

claims.text: TouchUp deliberately ignores ctx and skips ensureStream, so a release still goes out on a lost stream
claims.evidence: session.go:280-294 calls checkOpen only

stops.title: Type, and the keyboard the device is asked to believe in

claims.text: Type releases between characters so repeated characters do not collapse into one keypress
claims.evidence: TestTypeReleasesBetweenCharacters

claims.text: characters with no HID mapping are skipped with a warning rather than failing the call
claims.evidence: TestTypeSkipsCharactersWithNoMapping

claims.text: every leaf inside the storage block carries an explicit type tag, and the integer widths differ by position
claims.evidence: TestCreateKeyboardPayloadIntegerWidths and TestCreateKeyboardPayloadDeviceUsagePairs

claims.text: the report descriptor declared at registration does not describe the reports this package actually sends
claims.evidence: descriptor at payload.go:5-40 declares an 8-bit modifier plus 6-key array; BuildKeyboardReport sends a 240-bit bitmap at report.go:100-110

claims.text: CreateKeyboardService's missing-serviceID fallback may be reading a stale heartbeat reply left by earlier fire-and-forget reports, rather than a real omission by dtuhidd
claims.evidence: every SendReport sets HeartbeatRequestFlag and reads nothing; HeartbeatReplyFlag is defined at ios/xpc/encoding.go:45 and handled nowhere in the repo. Never decoded off the wire.
